purpose: Pemigatinib is used to treat certain types of bile duct cancer (called cholangiocarcinoma) in adults whose cancer has a specific gene change called an FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement. It is also used for some other rare cancers involving this same gene change. Your doctor will test your cancer to make sure this medicine is right for you.
how_it_works: Cancer cells sometimes have a faulty protein called FGFR2 that tells them to grow out of control. Pemigatinib works by blocking this faulty protein, which helps slow down or stop cancer cells from growing and spreading. Think of it like putting a lock on the switch that the cancer cells use to keep dividing.
common_side_effects: High phosphate levels in your blood (which your doctor will monitor), nail and skin changes, hair loss or thinning, dry eyes or mouth, diarrhea, constipation, tiredness, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, decreased appetite, mouth sores, and swelling in your hands or feet.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious eye problems, including vision changes or damage, so you will need regular eye check-ups. It can also cause dangerously high phosphate levels in your blood, which may require dietary changes or extra medication. Pemigatinib can harm an unborn baby, so use effective birth control during treatment and for some time afterward. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as some drugs can interact with pemigatinib.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 13.5 mg taken by mouth once a day for 14 days in a row, followed by 7 days off — this 21-day cycle then repeats. Take it with or without food, and swallow the tablet whole. Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have side effects or other health conditions.
